endorsement = public support for a product, often by a well-known person
target audience = the group of people an advert is designed to reach
misleading advert = an advertisement that gives a false or unclear impression
commercial = an advertisement on television or radio
billboard = a large outdoor board used to advertise a product
flyer = a small sheet of paper advertising an event or product
slogan = a short, memorable phrase used in advertising
jingle = a short, catchy tune used in a radio or TV advert
brand awareness = how well people recognise and remember a brand
product placement = showing a branded product in a film or programme as advertising
celebrity endorsement = when a famous person is paid to recommend a product
junk mail = unwanted advertising letters sent to your home
pop-up advert = an advert that appears suddenly on a website or app
classified ad = a short advertisement in a newspaper or website, often for jobs or goods
mailshot = a large number of advertising letters sent at the same time
cold calling = phoning people you do not know in order to sell something
hard sell = an aggressive way of trying to make someone buy at once
selling point = a feature that makes people want to buy one product rather than another
word of mouth = people recommending a product by talking about it
viral marketing = advertising designed to be shared quickly online
